housing.summary: Zug is Switzerland's wealthiest canton and has very high rents, driven by low taxes attracting corporations and high earners. Average 1-BR city-centre apartments run ~CHF 3,180/month per Numbeo (Jun 2026). Swiss law caps the rental deposit at 3 months' rent. Main portals: homegate.ch, comparis.ch, immoscout24.ch.

banking.summary: To open a bank account in Switzerland, residents need valid ID, proof of Swiss residence registration (Anmeldebestätigung), and permit (non-EU). Main banks in Zug: UBS, Zuger Kantonalbank (ZugerKB), and Raiffeisen. Zug is famous for attracting international blockchain and crypto companies, and specialist private banks operate locally.
required_docs: Employer letter or salary slip (sometimes required)

schools.summary: Zug has a strong international school sector. The International School of Zug and Lucerne (ISZL) is the main IB-accredited institution, serving international families. The canton's public schools are German-language. Several private and bilingual schools operate in the region.

legal_admin.summary: Newcomers must register at the Einwohnerkontrolle of their Zug municipality within 14 days of arrival. EU/EFTA nationals register for permit B or L at the Amt für Migration Kanton Zug. Non-EU nationals need a cantonal permit. Authority: sem.admin.ch.
legal_admin.registration_step: Anmeldung at Einwohnerkontrolle within 14 days; residence permit from cantonal migration authority

tax_finance.summary: The AHV-Nummer (OASI number) serves as the Swiss tax and social insurance ID, assigned by the SVA Zug (cantonal compensation office) or employer. Zug canton has Switzerland's lowest cantonal tax rates, making it a major draw for international businesses and wealthy individuals. Withholding tax applies for foreign residents without a C-permit.

transport.summary: Zug's public transport is operated by ZVB (Zugerland Verkehrsbetriebe), including buses and the Zug S-Bahn integrated into the cantons' network. A monthly pass costs approximately CHF 133 per Numbeo data (wider zone pass). EU/EFTA driving licences are exchangeable within 12 months at the Strassenverkehrsamt Kanton Zug without a driving test. Mandatory Krankenversicherung must be arranged within 3 months of arrival; regulated by BAG/OFSP.
transport.driving_licence_exchange: EU/EFTA licences exchangeable within 12 months at Strassenverkehrsamt Zug (sva-zg.ch/motorfahrzeuge); non-EU licences generally require theory and/or practical test
transport.healthcare_registration: Mandatory basic health insurance (Krankenversicherung/KVG) must be arranged within 3 months of arrival; choose a licensed insurer at bag.admin.ch
